text_blocks.snippet: The Supreme Court has recently issued several notable decisions affecting immigration law and policy. One recent ruling allows the Trump administration to resume deportations to third countries without providing 15 days' notice, potentially impacting individuals facing deportation who may have had limited opportunities to challenge their removal. Another decision allows the administration to circumvent district court rulings and strip legal status from certain migrants who entered the US under humanitarian parole, potentially affecting half a million individuals. These rulings highlight the ongoing legal battles and shifting interpretations surrounding immigration policy and the scope of presidential authority.
